title: Control Flow & Functions
relevance: Interviewers probe C conditionals, loops, and call semantics—especially pass-by-value versus pointers—because wrong models silently break swaps, scanf-style APIs, and recursion on the stack.

phases.goal: Establish how conditionals, loops, and function declarations control and organize program execution.

must_hit.point: An if evaluates an expression and runs its block when the result is non-zero (true); else is the fallback path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says non-zero means true and else covers the false/fallback case.

must_hit.point: switch evaluates an integer expression and jumps to a matching case label; cases must be compile-time integer constants.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions integer/constant cases and that strings, floats, or dynamic ranges are not valid switch targets.

must_hit.point: while checks the condition before each iteration (may never run); do-while checks after and guarantees at least one execution.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts pre-check vs post-check and names a do-while use like prompting until valid input.

must_hit.point: A for loop packs initialization, condition testing, and advancement on one line, suited to counting and array traversal.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes the three for-header parts and when for is preferred over while.

must_hit.point: A function prototype declares name, return type, and parameters; the definition supplies the body; void return means nothing returned and (void) means no parameters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Distinguishes declaration from definition and correctly explains void vs (void).

probes: Walk through how if/else and switch differ when you need to branch on many discrete constant values.
What is the difference between a while loop and a do-while loop?

hints.1: Start with how a condition decides whether a block runs.
hints.2: Compare branching constructs, then contrast pre-check vs post-check loops, then function declaration vs definition.
hints.3: if uses non-zero as true; switch needs compile-time integer cases; while may skip entirely while do-while always runs once; prototype announces the signature and definition holds the code.

phases.goal: Explain runtime mechanics of switch dispatch, loop control, pass-by-value, the call stack, and related function features.

must_hit.point: When case labels are dense, compilers like GCC and Clang can emit a jump table—an array of addresses indexed by the switch expression—for O(1) dispatch instead of sequential checks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names jump table, dense/contiguous cases, and O(1) indexed jump.

must_hit.point: C does not auto-exit a case; omitting break causes fallthrough into the next case.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly says fallthrough happens without break, unlike many other languages.

must_hit.point: C passes all function arguments by value: parameters are new locals initialized with copies of the caller's arguments; there is no built-in pass-by-reference.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States strictly pass-by-value and that same parameter names as callers are still separate variables.

must_hit.point: To mutate a caller's variable you pass a pointer by value; the address is copied, then the callee dereferences it to reach the original.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says the pointer itself is passed by value, and *p updates the caller's object.

must_hit.point: A call allocates a stack frame holding parameters, local variables, and the return address; on return the frame is popped and locals' automatic lifetime ends.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those three frame contents and that returning destroys the frame.

must_hit.point: Returning a pointer to a local creates a dangling pointer into reclaimed stack memory; dereferencing it is undefined behavior.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says never return &local because the frame is gone after return.

must_hit.point: Recursion needs a base case and a step toward it; each call pushes a frame, so deep recursion can exhaust the stack; C does not guarantee tail-call optimization into a loop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions base case, stack growth, and no guaranteed TCO in C.

must_hit.point: Variadic functions use ... with va_list/va_start/va_arg/va_end from stdarg.h and are type-unsafe: va_arg interprets memory as the requested type.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the stdarg macros and that wrong count/type yields undefined behavior.

probes: What lives in a stack frame, and why is returning a pointer to a local dangerous?
How can a dense switch be faster than a long if-else chain?

hints.1: Think about copies versus addresses, and what gets pushed when a function is called.
hints.2: Cover switch codegen (jump table/fallthrough), then argument copying and pointer simulation, then frame contents and dangling returns.
hints.3: No pass-by-reference—only pass-by-value; mutate via pointer; frames hold params, locals, return address; no break means fallthrough; dense cases can be O(1) via jump table.

phases.goal: Compare control-flow and function design choices the material presents as alternatives with clear costs.

must_hit.point: Long if-chains over many distinct constants become unreadable and an O(N) bottleneck; switch with dense cases can use a jump table for O(1) dispatch.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(N) if-chain vs O(1) jump-table switch when labels are dense.

must_hit.point: goto is discouraged for general logic but is a legitimate C idiom for centralized error cleanup because C lacks exceptions; jumping backward or across complex structure yields spaghetti.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defends goto for unwind/cleanup and warns against arbitrary jumps.

must_hit.point: Iterative loops usually use less memory than deep recursion, while recursive logic is often cleaner for tree-like structures; compilers may optimize tail recursion but C does not guarantee it.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Balances stack/memory cost of recursion against clarity, notes unguaranteed TCO.

must_hit.point: inline requests the compiler to inject the body to avoid call overhead for small hot functions, with type-checking unlike macros; the compiler may ignore inline for large, looping, or recursive bodies.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says inline is a request, good for tiny hot paths, silently ignored when unsuitable.

probes: When would you prefer switch over a long if-else chain, and when does switch fail?
When is goto acceptable in C, and when is recursion a bad fit versus a loop?

hints.1: Compare readability and cost of branching and of recursion versus loops.
hints.2: Tie if-chain linear checks to switch jump tables, then goto cleanup versus spaghetti, then recursion stack cost versus clarity.
hints.3: Dense integer cases favor switch/O(1) jump tables; if-chains are O(N); goto for error unwind only; recursion cleaner but stack-heavy with no guaranteed TCO; inline is optional for tiny functions.

phases.goal: Apply control-flow and calling conventions to concrete bugs, APIs, and traced examples from the material.

must_hit.point: broken_swap(int a, int b) only swaps the callee's copies; the caller's x and y are unchanged until you pass pointers and assign through *a/*b (e.g. *b = temp after *a = *b).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains why value-swap fails and shows pointer swap including *b = temp and callers passing &x, &y.

must_hit.point: scanf can modify caller variables because callers pass addresses; the function receives pointer copies and writes through them.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Links scanf to the pass-pointer-by-value pattern.

must_hit.point: Tracing factorial(3): frames push for 3 then 2 then 1; base returns 1; then 2*1=2 and 3*2=6 as frames pop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Narrates the push/pop order and final result 6.

must_hit.point: main is the entry point: int main(void) or int main(int argc, char **argv) with argv[0] as the program name; returning void is wrong—the int is the OS exit status (0 success, non-zero failure).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives both signatures, argv[0], and exit-status meaning.

must_hit.point: break exits only the innermost loop or switch; continue skips to the next iteration test—break does not escape multiple nested loops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects the nested-loop misconception and distinguishes continue.

must_hit.point: Using = instead of == in a condition (e.g. if (x = 5)) assigns and yields non-zero/true so the block always runs; -Wall helps catch this.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains accidental assignment and mentions compiler warnings with -Wall.

probes: Why does a swap function taking two ints fail, and how do you fix it?
If arguments are passed by value, how does scanf change the variables you pass?
Trace factorial(3) on the call stack.

hints.1: Apply pass-by-value to a concrete swap and to scanf.
hints.2: Fix swap with pointers, then connect scanf to addresses, then walk factorial(3) frame by frame.
hints.3: Value swap cannot change callers; use int* and *b = temp; scanf needs &var; factorial(3) yields 6 via nested frames; break is innermost-only; if (x = 5) always true.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: If-chains over many distinct constants are hard to read and check conditions sequentially in O(N). switch is cleaner for discrete compile-time integer constants; when cases are dense, compilers can build a jump table for O(1) dispatch. switch cannot match strings, floats, or dynamic ranges.

Recursion can express tree-like traversal cleanly with a base case and recursive step, but each call pushes a stack frame so deep recursion risks stack overflow. Loops usually use less memory. Some compilers turn tail recursion into a loop, but C does not guarantee that.

tradeoffs.topic: goto cleanup vs structured control flow
tradeoffs.strong_answer: goto is discouraged for general logic, but centralized error cleanup/unwinding is a standard C idiom because C has no exceptions. Using goto to jump backward or across complex structures produces spaghetti that is hard to follow.

tradeoffs.topic: inline function vs ordinary call (and vs macro)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: inline asks the compiler to paste the body at the call site to avoid call overhead, giving macro-like speed with real type-checking—useful for tiny, hot functions. For large, looping, or recursive bodies the compiler may ignore inline and emit a normal call.

gotchas.correction: Assignment stores 5 and the expression value is 5 (true), so the block always runs; enable -Wall for warnings.

gotchas.trap: Omitting break in a switch case.
gotchas.correction: Execution falls through into the next case; C does not auto-exit after a case.

gotchas.trap: Assuming switch can match strings, floats, or ranges.
gotchas.correction: switch requires compile-time integer constants only.

gotchas.trap: Off-by-one in a for loop over an array of size 10 using i <= 10.
gotchas.correction: Valid zero-based indices are 0 through 9; i <= 10 reads out of bounds (undefined behavior). Prefer i < 10.

gotchas.trap: Assuming break exits all nested loops.
gotchas.correction: break only terminates the innermost enclosing loop or switch.

gotchas.trap: Believing a parameter named like the caller's variable is linked to it.
gotchas.correction: They are separate locals; the parameter only starts with a copy of the argument value.

gotchas.trap: Implementing swap with void broken_swap(int a, int b).
gotchas.correction: Only the copies swap; pass int* and assign through *a and *b (e.g. *b = temp), calling with &x and &y.

gotchas.trap: Returning a pointer to a local variable.
gotchas.correction: The stack frame is destroyed on return, leaving a dangling pointer; dereferencing is undefined behavior.

gotchas.trap: Declaring main with a void return type.
gotchas.correction: main should return int as the process exit status: 0 for success, non-zero for failure.

gotchas.trap: Mismatched count or types for variadic arguments.
gotchas.correction: Variadic APIs are type-unsafe; va_arg blindly reinterprets memory, causing undefined behavior on mismatch.

gotchas.trap: Function pointer assigned with a mismatched signature.
gotchas.correction: Signature must match exactly; mismatch yields undefined behavior when called.

gotchas.trap: Looping on a hardware register without volatile.
gotchas.correction: The compiler may optimize the condition away and create an infinite loop; use volatile for such external state.
